question: What is the smallest schema-valid document and identity contract that all editors and codecs must preserve?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model, then widened it on 2026-10-04 to every existing ledger item. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was closed, with a latest pursue verdict, at queue position 1. It is not the unit next returned, which was reads.
requirements: One schema-valid immutable JSON document with primary children, optional object meta and named-root maps.
Every load path admits fields by input kind on the caller's raw object; no ingress silently drops or accepts a field another refuses (docs/vision/plite.md document top-level law).
A new top-level document field needs a doctrine change and a migration, because raw readers refuse unknown keys.
Plate migrations lift legacy top-level fields from a typed legacy channel; completion refuses a field no step lifted.
Runtime NodeKey, optional persisted element identity and schema lineage stay distinct.
Neutral model law stays in Plite; Plate construction, migrations and the CLI reuse it through plitejs/internal instead of copying it.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-10-04 review's arena, panel and editor comparison and the plan docs/plans/2026-10-03-model-document-admission.md (Status Done, uncommitted). Rechecked on the live tree the field lists and readers in document-shape.ts, every ingress call site via git grep (initial-value, editor-schema, public-state, compiled-slice-fitter, plugin, editor-runtime-view, authored/format, withPlite, documentMigrations, CLI), the owned-only view cache, the legacy types and completion refusal, and git status, which shows all of them staged and uncommitted. Did not rerun any test, probe or the CLI.
summary: The job is one schema-valid immutable JSON document (children, optional meta, named roots) that every load path admits the same way, with legacy top-level fields lifted only by explicit migration steps. Live source has the 2026-10-04 target. document-shape.ts holds one field list per input kind, each checked against its public type with satisfies, and readDocumentRecord on getEditorJsonRecordEntries refuses any other field. Construction, assertDocument, fitDocument, snapshot and envelope replace, the root-bound view, reconfigure and install migrate, Plate construction and Plate migrations all call those readers, and Plate reaches them through plitejs/internal. Migration steps receive a typed legacy record, completion refuses an unlifted field, and document views cache validation only for owned frozen documents. The strongest alternatives lose. Silent dropping (ProseMirror, Lexical, Tiptap) loses data that meta and migrations can carry, snapshotting caller documents per view pays a copy to guard caller misuse of an immutable model, and the 2026-10-04 distribution Pursue already covers the stray @internal root export setEditorSnapshotInputTransform. So keep the adopted design.

reconciliation.question: What is the smallest schema-valid document and identity contract that all editors and codecs must preserve?
reconciliation.reason: Its Pursue target is in the live tree at every ingress (document-shape.ts readers, legacy channel, owned-only view cache), and nothing materially better remains, so the verdict becomes Stop keeping that design. The adoption is uncommitted and its execution record is still pending.

alternatives: Keeping the adopted design wins. One reader and typed field lists cover every ingress, the legacy channel closes step documents, and no caller copies the law.

Dropping unknown top-level keys silently, as ProseMirror, Lexical, slate-v2 and Tiptap do, loses. Plite has meta for application data and a migration chain for legacy fields, so silent loss buys nothing.

Snapshotting (copying) a caller's document on every document-view admission to close post-admission mutation loses. The model is immutable, and a mutating caller is misusing it. The copy would add to the 21.7 ms per view the build already pays to revalidate a mutable 10,000-paragraph caller document, while owned documents such as editor.read.value() already skip both.

Deleting or moving setEditorSnapshotInputTransform off the public root under model is a real doctrine leak (an @internal value on the plitejs and platejs roots with no production caller). The 2026-10-04 distribution Pursue already owns all 16 @internal root values, so it does not reopen model.

A union-aware MigrationClosure, so a conditional or annotated step return fails to compile on an extra key, is additive type polish. Runtime already refuses the field at completion, so the benefit is earlier errors only.
A universal Plite-owned persisted identity or a public validated Document wrapper loses again. No consumer in the identity trace needs it, and raw Plite ingress must keep the same law.
